what: PDF to Text pulls all the words out of a PDF and shows them in a plain text box. From there you can copy the text or download it as a .txt file.

It is useful when you want to quote part of a report, paste a document into an email or a translator, search the words in another program, or reuse text that is hard to select in a PDF reader. It works on PDFs that contain real text, such as files made from Word or saved from a website.
The text is read inside your browser. The PDF is not sent anywhere.
uses: Copy text for an email or document
Take paragraphs from a PDF and paste them into Word, Google Docs or an email.
Extract the text and paste it into a translation tool.
The tool tells you how many words the PDF has, which helps with essays and articles.
Search and edit in a text editor
Save the text as .txt and open it in any editor to search, edit or reuse it.
Store a lightweight text version of a long PDF for quick searching later.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop a PDF here" or drag a PDF onto the box. The tool shows the file name and size, and the "Extract text" button becomes active.
The tool reads the PDF page by page and shows "Reading page 3 of 10…" while it works.

The text appears in the large box. Line breaks are kept where the PDF has them, and each page is separated from the next by an empty line. A green message shows the number of pages, the number of words and the size of the text.
Click "Copy" to copy everything in the box to your clipboard. You can also select part of the text in the box with your mouse or finger and copy only that.
Click "Download .txt" to save the text. The file has the same name as your PDF with .txt at the end, and it is saved in UTF-8 so letters from any language are kept.
features: Every page of the PDF is read in one click.
Copy all the text with one click.
Save the text as a plain UTF-8 file that opens anywhere.
See how many pages were read and how many words were found.
An empty line separates the text of each page, so you can see where pages end.
The text box cannot be changed by accident, so what you copy matches the PDF.

example.title: Worked example: quoting a research report
example.text: Daniel has climate-report.pdf with 12 pages and wants to quote the summary on page 2. He loads the file and clicks "Extract text". The message shows "12 pages, 4,830 words". He scrolls to the summary in the text box, selects the paragraph he needs and copies it into his essay. He also clicks "Download .txt" to save climate-report.txt for later.

tips: If the PDF is a scan, this tool finds no text. You need an OCR app to turn pictures of text into real text.
Text from two-column layouts may come out with the columns mixed. Check the order before you use it.
Tables come out as plain lines of text. You may need to tidy them up by hand.
Paste the text into a plain editor first if you want to remove all formatting.
If the PDF is password protected, remove the password first.
problems: The message says "No text was found"
The PDF is probably a scan or a photo, which holds a picture of text instead of real text. This tool cannot read pictures.
The text has strange symbols or broken words
Some PDFs use fonts that do not store which letter is which. The text cannot be read correctly from those files.
The words are in the wrong order
The order comes from how the PDF was made. Columns, sidebars and text boxes can be stored in a different order than they appear.
It only appears after text has been found. Click "Extract text" first.
